story: Enoch, son of the patriarch Jared, was father of Methuselah. He lived 365 years, walking with God, until God took him so that he was no more and did not experience death like other ancestors. Traditions say he was raised to heaven and appointed guardian of celestial treasures, made chief of the angels, and set as an attendant before God's throne. There he was taught all secrets and mysteries, and with angels at his command he carried out whatever God decreed. He was identified as the being who communicates God's word, and through this role he was said to have conveyed divine revelation to Moses and dictated the Book of Jubilees. He was also given the title of "Great Scribe" for his piety. One tradition holds that though righteous, he was easily tempted toward evil, so God took him away before his time to preserve his righteousness. Another story tells that the earth had been corrupted by the demons Shammazai and Azazel, and Enoch was carried to heaven to demonstrate that God was not cruel. A further account describes him as a pious ascetic who preached repentance, gathered many disciples despite the world's small population, and was made king; under his rule peace reigned until he was summoned to heaven to govern the sons of God. In another version, he founded an exceedingly righteous city named Zion; its entire people were taken to heaven without dying, due to their piety. He also foretold that his descendant Noah would survive a great flood with his family, preserving mankind and sacred writings. He performed miracles and witnessed wars and disasters in his lifetime.
